Claims, models, and comparisons are the public objects in `geap`. A
claim has cash-flow dynamics, which you either measure from data or
write down. A model prices a set of named claims, and a comparison
sets two priced claims side by side. The model prices claims, and you
choose which pair to report as a spread.

```python
import geap

model = geap.LongRunRisksModel()
res = model.solve()
print(res.summary())

cmp = res.compare("value", "growth", market="market")
cmp.premium
```

<!-- Cross-checked against `geap.__all__`. New public names belong here
     in the same pull request. -->

## Protocol

Each asset-pricing family subclasses the protocol types in the table,
and long-run risks is the first family in the package.

| Name | Role |
|:---|:---|
| `AssetPricingModel` | Immutable specification. `solve`, optional `simulate`, `replace`. |
| `AssetPricingResults` | `summary`, `to_frame`, `compare`. |
| `Comparison` | Long minus short in the results' headline measure. |
| `Summary` | Formatted text table. |

## Claims

`ClaimParams` stores the parameters of one claim, and a claim has four
parameters in total. Only $\phi$, the loading on persistent consumption
growth, differs across claims in a cross-section.

| Function | Signature | Returns |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `ClaimParams` | `(mu, phi, phi_sigma, alpha)` | the parameters of one claim |
| `ClaimParams.from_loading` | `(phi, *, mu=0.0015, phi_sigma=7.5, alpha=0.5)` | a synthetic claim that differs from another only in $\phi$ |
| `calibrate_claim` | `(dc, dd, *, frequency="annual", window=2, default_phi_sigma=7.5)` | one `ClaimParams` measured from cash flows |
| `calibrate_claims` | `(dc, claims, **kw)` | a whole cross-section, one `calibrate_claim` each |

Neither calibration function has an argument for a return, so the
premium the model produces later is a prediction rather than a fit.

```python
value = geap.calibrate_claim(dc, dd_value)
claims = geap.calibrate_claims(dc, {"value": dd_v, "growth": dd_g,
                                   "market": dd_m})
mine = geap.ClaimParams.from_loading(1.5)
```

## The model

| Member | Signature | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `LongRunRisksModel` | `(params=None, *, delta=None, gamma=None, psi=None, mu=None, rho=None, phi_x=None, sigma=None, nu=None, sigma_w=None, claims=None, residual_corr=None)` | The specification. Defaults to Table II. |
| `.solve` | `(method="grid", *, n_x=30, n_s=4, max_iter=200_000, tol=1e-10, pd_anchor=None, pd_anchor_c=None)` | `GridResults` or `AnalyticalResults` |
| `.simulate` | `(n_samples=1000, years=74, *, seed=0, burn_in_years=5, n_x=30, n_s=4)` | `SimulationResults`: the paper's Table VII |
| `.simulate_cashflows` | `(n_sims=200, years=74, seed=42)` | cash-flow moments only, no prices (Tables III to V) |
| `.simulate_paths` | `(months, *, seed=None)` | one simulated path of $x_t$, $\sigma_t^2$, and growth rates |
| `.replace` | `(**kwargs)` | a new model with some arguments changed |
| `.claims` | property | claim names, in order |

## Estimation (Bansal, Kiku, and Yaron 2016)

Everything below lives in `geap.lrr.estimation`. The four pages
[Estimation](estimation.qmd), [Time aggregation](time-aggregation.qmd),
[Size and book-to-market claims](portfolios.qmd), and [Post-war
quarterly data](quarterly.qmd) use these names and nothing else.

### Solution and moments

| Member | Signature | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `BKYParams` | `(gamma, psi, delta, mu_c, rho, phi_e, sigma, nu, sigma_w, mu_d, phi_d, phi_d_sigma, rho_d)` | the thirteen decision-frequency parameters |
| `LogLinearSolution` | dataclass | affine loadings of the consumption and market claims, the risk-free rate, and the risk prices |
| `solve_loglinear` | `(params)` | appendix A affine solution at the decision frequency |
| `model_moments` | `(params, h, sol=None)` | time-aggregated moments at `h` decisions per sampling interval |
| `long_run_variance_share` | `(params, h)` | share of aggregated consumption variance from the persistent component |
| `extract_states` | `(log_pd, rf, sol, *, params=None, h=1, sigma2_floor=1e-10, ar=True)` | latent expected growth and variance from the price-dividend ratio and the risk-free rate |

### Data

| Member | Signature | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `load_annual` | `(path=None, *, start=1930, end=2015)` | shipped 1930 to 2015 annual sample |
| `load_quarterly` | `(path=None, *, start=1948, end=2015)` | shipped 1948 to 2015 quarterly sample |
| `load_cross_section` | `(path=None)` | shipped size and book-to-market quintile legs |
| `build_annual` | `(path=None, *, refresh=False)` | rebuild the annual sample from CRSP, BLS, and BEA (needs WRDS) |
| `sample_moments` | `(data)` | Table 1 descriptive statistics |

### Estimator

| Member | Signature | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `estimate_bky` | `(data, *, h=None, h_grid=None, start=None, stochastic_vol=True, method="gmm", W="cue_invvar", j_test=True, hac_lags=1, n_boot=0, block_length=8, maxiter=800, bootstrap_h=False, start_is_monthly=True, n_starts=1)` | CUE GMM with `h` chosen on a grid; `n_starts` keeps the lowest objective of several generic starts |
| `BKYResults` | `params, h, gmm, data, stochastic_vol` | the fit; `summary()`, `table2_frame(paper=, paper_se=, paper_h=)`, `states()`, `moment_table()`, `model` |
| `COLD_START` | `BKYParams` | the Bansal and Yaron (2004) monthly start |
| `estimate_table7_claims` | `(panel, market_params=None, h=11)` | second-stage cash-flow vectors of the four portfolios at the market states |
| `table4_annual_on_lrr_sims` | `(n_draws=20, years=86, seed=0, *, lrr_params=None, lrr_h=None, n_starts=1)` | the annual specification on simulated LRR samples |

### Tables and figures

| Member | Signature | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `table1_frame` | `(data)` | Table 1, ours beside the paper's |
| `params_frame` | `(res, *, paper, paper_se=None, paper_h=None, paper_j=None)` | one estimated column with the printed vector and SEs |
| `table2_frame` | `(lrr, novol)` | Table 2, both models |
| `table3_frame`, `table5_frame` | `(data, params, h, *, hac_lags=1)` | sample, model, and $t$(diff) |
| `table3_compare` | `(data, res, paper_model, *, hac_lags=1)` | Table 3 or 5 with the paper's model column |
| `table4_frame` | `(ann, mc=None)` | Table 4, empirical and simulated columns |
| `table6_frame` | `(fits)` | Table 6 from fits keyed by `h` |
| `table7_claims`, `table7_premia`, `table7_capm` | `(market=None, h=11, *, claims=None, ...)` | the paper's Panel A vectors, model premia, and simulated CAPM betas |
| `table7_panel_a`, `table7_panel_b` | `(claims, panel, market, h)`, `(claims, market, h, panel, annual, *, years=2000, seed=1)` | Table 7 panels with the paper's values |
| `table8_frame` | `(ta, no_ta)` | Table 8 |
| `figure1_frame`, `figure1_long`, `figure1_ggplot` | `(data, params=None, h=None)`, `(frame)`, `(frame)` | Figure 1 states, tidy frame, plotnine figure |
| `figure2_irf`, `figure2_long`, `figure2_ggplot` | `(*, horizon_dc=50, horizon_var=150, years=800, seed=0, lrr_params=None, lrr_h=None, annual_params=None)`, `(irf)`, `(irf)` | Figure 2 impulse responses, tidy frame, plotnine figure |

### Printed values

`TABLE_2_LRR`, `TABLE_2_LRR_H`, `TABLE_2_SE`, `TABLE_2_NOVOL`,
`TABLE_2_NOVOL_H`, `TABLE_3_LRR_MODEL`, `TABLE_3_LRR_RESIDUALS`,
`TABLE_3_NOVOL_MODEL`, `TABLE_3_NOVOL_RESIDUALS`, `TABLE_4_ANNUAL`,
`TABLE_5_ANNUAL_MODEL`, `TABLE_5_ANNUAL_RESIDUALS`, `TABLE_8_TA`, and
`TABLE_8_H` are the paper's printed cells, pinned for comparison. The
rest of the printed tables live in `geap.lrr.estimation.goldens`.

`method="grid"` solves the Euler equations on the Tauchen-Hussey state
space, and `method="analytical"` is the log-linear approximation of
Section 3.4.

```python
geap.LongRunRisksModel(gamma=7.5).solve().compare("value", "growth").premium
model.replace(claims={"value": {"phi": 2.6}}).solve().compare("value", "growth").premium
```

If you pass a claim with only some of its four fields filled in, the
remaining fields stay at their calibrated values. Naming a claim
absent from the default replaces the whole cross-section, and then all
four fields are required.

## Results

Quantities that vary by claim are `pandas.Series` indexed by claim
name, and returns, premia, and rates are annualized and in percent.

| Attribute | On | Meaning |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `expected_returns`, `volatility`, `sharpe_ratios` | grid, simulation | annual return moments by claim |
| `mean_log_pd`, `price_dividend` / `pd_levels` | all three | valuation ratios by claim |
| `risk_free` | all three | the rate, which follows from the SDF and needs no claim |
| `capm_betas(market)` | grid, simulation | betas of every claim against the reference you name |
| `beta_matrix`, `return_cov` | grid, simulation | betas and covariances for every pair |
| `converged`, `n_x`, `n_s` | grid | how the solve went |
| `z_c`, `z`, `stationary`, `x_nodes`, `s2_nodes`, `states()` | grid | the solved valuation functions and the grid under them |
| `A1`, `A2`, `long_run_premium`, `expected_growth`, `gordon_return` | analytical | loadings and the long-run piece of compensation |
| `risk_prices`, `Lambda_eta`, `Lambda_eps`, `Lambda_w` | analytical | prices of the three shocks |
| `expected_returns_se`, `volatility_se`, `mean_log_pd_se` | simulation | cross-sample dispersion |
| `summary()` | all three | a formatted table |
| `to_frame()` | all three | a tidy frame, one row per claim |

`capm_betas` is a method rather than an attribute, because a beta
needs a reference claim. `to_frame()` and `states()` follow the
`tidyfinance` backend.

## Comparison

`res.compare(long, short, market=None)` sets two priced claims side by
side, and the market argument is only needed for betas.

| Attribute | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| `premium` | long minus short: expected return on a grid or simulated solve, long-run risk premium on an analytical one |
| `log_pd_spread` | long minus short mean log P/D |
| `volatility_spread` | long minus short volatility; NaN on analytical results |
| `betas`, `beta_ratio` | the two legs' betas against `market`, and their ratio |
| `label` | "Value premium" for a value and growth pair, else "Long-short premium" |
| `summary()` | the two legs and the spreads between them |
| `to_frame()` | one tidy row, for stacking across a sweep |

On simulated results `beta_ratio` is the cross-sample mean of the
per-sample ratio, which is the quantity the paper reports. The
attribute is not the ratio of the reported mean betas.

## Measure loadings from cash flows

| Function | Signature | Returns |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `expected_growth_proxy` | `(dc, window=2) -> ndarray` | moving average of lagged consumption growth |
| `filter_expected_growth` | `(dc) -> dict` | Kalman/MLE $\hat x_t$; `mu, rho, q, r, loglik, x` |
| `estimate_long_run_leverage` | `(dc, dd, window=2) -> float` | $\tilde\phi$: slope of cash-flow growth on the MA |

## Data construction

| Function | Signature | Returns |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `load_consumption` | `() -> pd.Series` | real per-capita ND+S growth, 1930 to 2003 |
| `load_deflator` | `() -> pd.Series` | PCE deflator |
| `real_rf_from_monthly` | `(t90, cpi) -> pd.Series` | annual real T-bill from monthly |
| `campbell_shiller_annual` | `(ret, retx, defl) -> pd.DataFrame` | real dividends and price index from CRSP returns |
| `build_annual_panel` | `(refresh=False, start=1930, end=2003) -> pl.DataFrame` | growth/value/market panel |
| `table_i` | `(bm, start=1930, end=2003) -> pd.DataFrame` | Table I statistics |
| `table_vi_data` | `(bm, dc, start=1930, end=2003) -> pd.DataFrame` | Table VI loadings |
| `EmpiricalDataError` | exception | raised when WRDS credentials are missing |

## Parameters and errors

`ModelParams()`, `PreferencesParams`, `ConsumptionParams`, and
`ClaimParams` are the parameter dataclasses, and `ModelParams()` is
the Table II calibration. `SolverDivergenceError` is raised when a
fixed point leaves the plausible range, and `EmpiricalDataError` is
raised when WRDS credentials are missing.

The long-run risks family is in `geap.lrr`, and public calibration and
empirical helpers are re-exported at the `geap` root.

## A new sort, end to end

You pass in consumption growth and one cash-flow series per claim, and
you do not pass returns at any point.

```python
import polars as pl
import geap

dc = pl.read_csv("data/consumption_annual.csv").sort("year")["dc"].to_numpy()
panel = pl.read_csv("data/annual_panel.csv")

def dd(claim):
    return (
        panel.filter(pl.col("claim") == claim)
        .sort("year")["dgrowth"]
        .to_numpy()
    )

claims = geap.calibrate_claims(
    dc,
    {"value": dd("Value"), "growth": dd("Growth"), "market": dd("Market")},
    frequency="annual",
    window=2,
)
res = geap.LongRunRisksModel(claims=claims).solve()
print(res.compare("value", "growth", market="market").summary())
```

The premium the model returns was never targeted, so a comparison with
the data is a test rather than a fit.
